thread.title: Spotify finds defenders after shares sink on earnings

author: Emily Bary
title: Spotify finds defenders after shares sink on earnings
text:
Spotify Technology SA faced the music late Wednesday with its first earnings report as a public company, which sent shares down 8.4% after the numbers fell short of consensus estimates.
But analysts took an extra beat to unpack why the results came as such a negative surprise. After all, Spotify SPOT, -7.19% had updated its outlook toward the end of the first quarter. Revenue actually came in at the high end of the company’s forecasted range.
“All in, these should have been exactly as-expected results,” wrote RBC Capital Markets analyst Mark Mahaney.
“We would have been disappointed with upside as we felt it would have damaged credibility of guidance going forward,” MKM analyst Rob Sanderson wrote. “We were pleased to see gross margin at the higher end and solid outlook.”
See more: Apple is no threat, says Spotify CEO
One negative, Mahaney pointed out, was that the company’s average revenue per user for its paid service came in at €4.72, below his €4.82 estimate. That was the result of continued interest in family plans, which let multiple users pack onto a single account for just a bit more than the cost of one standalone membership, as well as foreign-exchange headwinds.
“Management guided to diminishing mix-shift pressure as the company anniversaries plan rollouts,” Mahaney wrote of the ARPU metric. He cut his price target to $210 from $220 following the release, which made him the only analyst to reduce his target. Three other analysts raised theirs.
Of the 19 analysts who cover Spotify, 13 have buy ratings, five have hold ratings and one has a sell rating, according to FactSet. The average price target is $179.28, 5.5% above current levels.
Some analysts discussed Spotify’s plan to upgrade its free service and give those listeners access to more songs on demand. “With a new and ostensibly more-engaging free product creating volume growth at the top of the user funnel, multiple new market launches expected for the rest of the year, and continued strength in macro drivers like smartphones and smart speakers, we see a robust outlook for audience growth and therefore for the stock,” wrote Canaccord Genuity analyst Maria Ripps, who rates the stock a buy with a $200 price target.
Read more: When will we get to choose our voice assistant?
Evercore ISI analyst Anthony DiClemente took a look at Spotify’s subscriber growth rates, which accelerated in all regions except for North America. “A cautious interpretation here could be that competitive pressures from Apple Inc. AAPL, -0.82% are having an impact in North America at the margin,” DiClemente wrote. Spotify extended the length of free trials on a “temporary” basis during the quarter, he said.
Spotify Chief Executive Daniel Ek dismissed concerns about competition during the company’s earnings call. “We don’t see any kind of meaningful impact of competition,” he said. “In fact, when we look at this, we don’t really think that this is a winner-takes-all market.”
DiClemente left his outperform rating and $190 price target intact following the results. “The simple fact is that Spotify maintains the fastest user growth of any platform in our coverage,” he wrote. DiClemente also follows Match Group Inc. MTCH, +5.18% Facebook Inc. FB, -1.34% Snap Inc. SNAP, -2.03% and Pandora Media Inc. P, -0.98% among other names.
Spotify shares are down 7.3% from their opening price of $165.90 a month ago, when the company went public via a direct listing. The S&P SPX, -1.03% is down 0.5% in the past month.
